## Motivation `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` runs DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1 sparse attention through FlashInfer's trtllm-gen sparse MLA kernel (added in #30805). This PR makes that backend accurate with every feature DeepSeek-V4.1 serving uses (DSpark speculative decoding, DP attention, decoder and encoder SWA bounded replay, CUDA graphs) and removes the work SGLang did around each kernel call, so the backend is faster end to end, not only per call. - **Metadata in the kernel's own form**, as TRT-LLM integrates it: one persistent table per step holds every token's sliding-window and sparse KV slots, and decode, verify, draft-extend and prefill all pass one query row per token. - **KV cache in the uniform FP8 layout the kernel reads**, written by SGLang's fused norm-RoPE kernels, which also emit the FP8 query directly. - **Little glue around each call:** a persistent counter buffer instead of a zero-fill before every call, the DSpark draft step's metadata inside its CUDA graph, KV stores that read strided inputs instead of copies, and an indexer that writes its top-k straight into the shared table. **Impact** - **Accuracy: unchanged vs FlashMLA.** GPQA-Diamond 0.907 vs 0.909; paired difference -0.25 points, 95% CI [-1.39, +0.76]; DSpark accept length 3.23 vs 3.26 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GB300 TP4, sgl-eval, 198 questions x 4, real acceptance). The registered GB300 e2e tests pass. - **Performance: faster than FlashMLA at aggregated TP, and faster than main's trtllm-gen at every point measured.** Per-request decode time on published InferenceX AgentX recipes, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash with DSpark (negative = this PR is faster): | Point | vs FlashMLA | vs main's trtllm-gen | |---|---|---| | GB300 TP4 c1 | -0.95% | | | GB300 TP4 c16 | -0.8% to -1.3% | | | B300 TP2 c48 | -1.7% | -2.2% | | GB200 TP4 c32 | -2.2% | -5.1% | | B300 DEP2 c64 | | -2.5% | Against FlashMLA Mega, the published backend at the DEP points: ahead at GB300 DEP2 c64 (output tok/s +2.5% to +4.6%), behind at B300 DEP2 c64 (p90 interactivity -2.3%, output tok/s tie). ## Modifications **+874 / −506 runtime code (20 files), +895 / −113 tests (7 files), +6 docs (1 file).** Kernel changes are edits to existing SGLang JIT kernels (fused norm-RoPE and KV store, top-k, metadata); no new kernels. - **trtllm backend** (`deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py`): the persistent table pool, refreshed per step (the indexed tail only on index-source layers); dense per-token calls; a persistent multi-CTA counter buffer; PDL off only for an attention launch right after a tail refresh (the kernel reads lengths before `griddepcontrol.wait`); decode tables sized for the adaptive-spec max draft width; `--dsv4-trtllm-flashinfer-backend {trtllm-gen,auto}` (default `trtllm-gen`; `auto` lets FlashInfer pick and logs the result at startup). - **Shared DeepSeek-V4 metadata** (`deepseek_v4_backend.py`, `dsv4/metadata.py`, `metadata_kernel.py`): trtllm tables for speculative decoding and DP attention built inside the captured metadata graphs, the DSpark draft step included; late-layer tail tables for decoder SWA bounded replay; encoder SWA bounded replay; the low-ratio metadata kernel writes trtllm's lengths; no per-step padding or refills of table rows the kernel never reads; no self-copies of pool-backed tables. - **KV store and query** (`fused_norm_rope_v2.cuh`, `main_norm_rope.cuh`, `norm_rope.py`, `compress.py`, `compressor_v2.py`, `deepseek_v4.py`): a uniform-FP8 store variant of the fused norm-RoPE and compressor kernels, replacing the separate `compressor_trtllm.py` path; FP8 queries from the fused query norm-RoPE kernel; no FlashMLA query-head padding on the trtllm path. - **KV pools** (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py`, `dsv41_request_window.py`, `dsv4_request_window_copy.py`): uniform-FP8 pools, including the encoder-replay request window. - **Indexer and DSpark** (`topk_v2.cuh`, `deepseek_v4_dspark.py`): the top-k kernel takes a row stride so it writes the shared table in place; the DSpark commit-KV store reads the stacked projection's strided slices. - **Tests:** counter buffer and the PDL edge in a captured graph, bitwise metadata and in-place-tail checks, the uniform-FP8 fused store, and a GB300 encoder-replay e2e test; each fails on a mutant of the code it covers. The stale manual VarSeq prefill test is removed. ## Accuracy Tests GPQA-Diamond with sgl-eval 0.1.3, 198 questions x 4 repeats, the model's preset with reasoning effort max (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking on). DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 node, TP4, DSpark (block 5) with real acceptance, 64 concurrent requests; same build and flags in both runs, only `--dsv4-attn-backend` differs. | `--dsv4-attn-backend` | pass@1 (mean of 4) | per repeat | majority@4 | DSpark accept length | |---|---|---|---|---| | flashmla | 0.909 | 0.914 / 0.904 / 0.909 / 0.909 | 0.912 | 3.26 | | trtllm | 0.907 | 0.909 / 0.904 / 0.919 / 0.894 | 0.914 | 3.23 | Paired per-question difference (trtllm - flashmla): -0.25 points, 95% bootstrap CI [-1.39, +0.76] over the 198 questions. All 792 samples per run finished with `stop`; none were truncated. ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 --max-running-requests 64 --prefill-decode-interval 0 \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \ --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \ --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --tokenizer-backend fastokens \ --dsv4-attn-backend {flashmla|trtllm} sgl-eval run gpqa --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --n-repeats 4 --num-threads 64 --load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --reasoning-effort max ``` Registered GB300 e2e tests, real DSpark acceptance (`test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300_trtllm_bounded_bcg.py` and `..._encoder_bcg.py`; thresholds GSM8K 0.95, MMMU-Pro 0.75): bounded BCG GSM8K-200 0.98, MMMU-Pro-200 0.77, accept length 3.33; encoder replay BCG 0.97 / 0.78 / 3.28 (run on this head's code plus #46835's value-preserving copy skip). The unit tests the PR touches pass on B300.
Earlier accuracy checks (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, older heads) GPQA: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \ --dsv4-attn-backend trtllm \ --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \ --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --disable-flashinfer-autotune \ --chat-template ./chat_template.jinja \ --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 128 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 21000 ``` Eval: ```bash python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 21000 --eval-name gpqa \ --num-examples 198 --max-tokens 120000 --repeat 8 \ --thinking-mode deepseek-v3 ``` flashmla (baseline, no MTP): ``` Repeat: 8, mean: 0.885 Scores: ['0.889', '0.879', '0.889', '0.879', '0.869', '0.899', '0.904', '0.874'] ``` trtllm_gen (same server command with --dsv4-attn-backend trtllm; same eval command): ``` Repeat: 8, mean: 0.907 Scores: ['0.919', '0.904', '0.894', '0.904', '0.909', '0.919', '0.904', '0.904'] ``` Extra stress testing: - DP4+MTP: GSM8K 0.975 - DP4+MTP stress: 128/128 requests; accepted length 1.99; no IMA - DP4 non-MTP: GSM8K 0.970 - DP4 non-MTP stress: 128/128 requests; no IMA - Focused metadata/output tests: 12 passed
## Speed Tests and Profiling **AgentX** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DSpark block 5): the published InferenceX recipe for each point, including its simulated acceptance; arms on one node with a fresh server per run, the same tree and image, only the attention backend different; per-request decode is the paired median ms/token per request. Methods, per-block tables, accuracy and noise: [GB300 c1 / c16](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36652#issuecomment-6429448233), [B300 / GB200 points](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36652#issuecomment-6441524741). These were measured before the last metadata trims, which cut a further ~30 µs per decode step at GB300 TP4 c1 (40-step torch profile; not re-measured end to end).
Kernel traces (older head) Traces show there are no extra "glue" kernels added (FlashMLA has splitKV + combine kernel, which is why it's total kernel count for the selected decode slice is 1 more), and we can confirm the individual kernel perf (in this case, ~13µs -> 10µs). FlashMLA: TRTLLM-Gen:

FlashMLA Mega vs this PR at GB300 DEP2 c64 (nightly 20261016) **trtllm-gen (this PR) is 2.5–4.6% faster than MegaAttention (`flashmla_mega`, #43922) in output tok/s. Its ITL p50 is about 4.5% lower.** | Setting | Value | |---|---| | Model | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | | Hardware | One server on 2× GB300 (AIHub oci-jhb) | | Workload | AgentX: `agentx-harness` 1.0.7 on `semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126`, concurrency 64, 900 s measured after warmup | | Server | InferenceX `override_dep2_c64` recipe: TP2 / DP-attention 2 / EP2, MegaMoE, DSpark block 5 with simulated accept length 3.51, HiCache | | Arms | Same tree (`2bb155af0e`: this PR plus main, which includes #43922). The arms differ only in `--dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega` vs `trtllm`. Mega uses NVFP4 KV and trtllm uses FP8 KV. | | Prefill CUDA graphs | Mega out tok/s | trtllm out tok/s | trtllm vs Mega | ITL p50 Mega / trtllm | |---|---|---|---|---| | disabled (4 runs per arm) | 2,496 | 2,611 | **+4.6%** | 7.52 / 7.20 ms | | breakable, recipe default (Mega 3 runs, trtllm 4) | 2,520 | 2,582 | **+2.5%** | 7.51 / 7.16 ms | - **Paired runs:** trtllm won all 5 pairs run back to back on the same node, by 2.2% to 4.2%. The ITL ranges don't overlap: every trtllm run falls between 7.09 and 7.27 ms, every Mega run between 7.35 and 7.67 ms. TTFT p50 is 2–4% lower for trtllm on average. All 15 runs had 0 errors. - **Comparison with #43922:** our Mega result reproduces the Mega number in #43922 (2,523 tok/s). This PR's trtllm is about 13% faster than main's trtllm in that PR's table (2,315 tok/s), which reverses its ranking. - **Where Mega loses:** its decode step is 2.5–5% slower at the same batch size, measured from the server logs. Mega also spends about 268 µs per prefill call unpacking its NVFP4 cache. - **Why NVFP4's smaller KV cache doesn't help here:** KV capacity is not the limit at concurrency 64 (prefix-cache hit rate about 93%, peak device KV usage 0.34 Mega / 0.24 trtllm). In addition, main sizes Mega's pool too small: 15.3M tokens per rank vs trtllm's 19.4M. - **Not covered:** - Encoder SWA bounded replay was off on both arms. trtllm support for it was added to this PR afterwards (be05f7a). - Only concurrency 64 / DEP2 was run. - Speculative acceptance was simulated, per the recipe.

Before this update, on the same recipe: the PR measured +3.78% [+3.47, +4.13] per-request decode time vs FlashMLA, and +2.26% [+1.80, +2.60] with the counter-buffer fix alone (other nodes, same harness).

+every attention launch, so outputs must equal FlashInfer's per-call counters bit

+    return torch.full((64, *shape), fill, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")

+    """Capture fn (never replayed); for each edge into an attention (fmha)
+    kernel, whether it is programmatic. The DOT dump prints no edge types."""
+    from cuda.bindings import driver
+
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph(keep_graph=True)
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        fn()
+    get_edges = ctypes.CDLL("libcuda.so.1").cuGraphGetEdges_v2
+    get_edges.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] * 4 + [ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_size_t)]
+    handle, num = graph.raw_cuda_graph(), ctypes.c_size_t(0)
+    assert get_edges(handle, None, None, None, ctypes.byref(num)) == 0
+    src, dst = (ctypes.c_void_p * num.value)(), (ctypes.c_void_p * num.value)()
+    data = ((ctypes.c_uint8 * 8) * num.value)()  # CUgraphEdgeData: byte 2 = type
+    assert get_edges(handle, src, dst, data, ctypes.byref(num)) == 0

[by Claude Code] **Severity: perf | Confidence: High**

**Issue**
This change makes the earlier `p_c128` memory concern (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36652#discussion_r4144572150) larger. `p_c128` is now allocated at startup with `max_prefill_rows` rows at full-context width. `_trtllm_query_row_capacity` includes `--max-prefill-tokens` (default 16384), so a smaller `--chunked-prefill-size` does not shrink it. The KV pool is sized before this runs, so the memory comes out of activation headroom.

**Example**
With a 1M context, each row is ~8.4K int32 (~33.8 KB). 16384 rows hold ~554 MB per rank on every server, even with `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`. The old lazy parent grew only to the largest chunk (~138 MB at 4096 rows).

**Fix**
Keep `p_c128` lazy, and back it with flat storage viewed as `buf[: rows * width].view(rows, width)` with this chunk's `SWA_WINDOW + w128`.
